H-OS-L1.name: Pebble
H-OS-L1.sphere: n=95, mean=7.15, std=1.78, confidence=strong. Strong peak in overstimulation cluster with 66% pct_pos and the only protocol at n ≥ 90 in this run. Qualitative: mode is noticeable improvement (12) within 10-minute settle (11), with 19 of 29 music responses liked or loved. AutoGluon predicts 6.859 — approximately 0.3 below observed, indicating good but not exceptional model capture. YouTube views=30 — highest in dataset, suggesting organic discoverability alongside strong empirical signal.
H-OS-L1.sphere_plain: The most-used overstimulation protocol in the library and a strong all-rounder. Most listeners feel clearer and more grounded quickly, and the music consistently earns high marks.

H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall
H-OS-L2.sphere: n=51, mean=6.92, std=1.73, confidence=strong. 65% pct_pos with moderate variance. Qualitative: 10-minute settle as mode (10), 10 of 21 'liked' music and 6 neutral. Rhythm opinion evenly split between 'very settling' (7) and 'balanced' (7). Cross-volume stability hinted at via strong confidence under single-volume observation. Drift sim=0.780. YouTube views=5 — discovery lags despite strong internal rating.
H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Works well for sensory overload and a good mid-length choice. Listener experiences are consistently positive, though the rhythm draws slightly more divided feedback than the first in the set.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier
H-OS-L3.sphere: n=47, mean=7.04, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful. 64% pct_pos and, unusually, 10 'very settling' rhythm ratings alongside 10 'balanced' — a bimodal qualitative signal matching its analytical isolation (mean_sim=0.677). Qualitative shows 7 settle in 5 minutes and 'Trying to sleep' as a leading activity (8 of 23). Drift sim=0.679. YouTube views=8.
H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Especially strong for settling overstimulated minds and finding sleep. The rhythm is described as both balanced and deeply settling — sometimes by the same listeners.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow
H-AX-L1.sphere: n=67, mean=7.22, std=1.93, confidence=strong. Distribution skews positive with 63% pct_pos and the highest among H-AX protocols. Qualitative: 13 self-listeners, 6 client/patient-users, strong preference for balanced rhythm (13) and 10-minute settle time (9). AutoGluon routes X-ME-L1 and X-MD-L1 here, predicting 7.838 — approximately 0.6 above observed, suggesting modest latent upside if those subpopulations are guided here. YouTube views=7 with no retention data — reach too low for conclusions.
H-AX-L1.sphere_plain: A strong and well-tested protocol for anxiety and stress. Most listeners feel meaningful calm take hold within about ten minutes, and the music tends to land well across the board.

H-AX-L2.name: Cottage
H-AX-L2.sphere: n=48, mean=6.94, std=1.62, confidence=meaningful. Tighter distribution than L1 (std lower) with 67% pct_pos and a long tail toward 8. Qualitative: 20 responses lean toward self-listeners (12), settle-time mode at 5 minutes (9), music opinion split (9 liked, 5 neutral). Drift sim=0.652 — moderate analytical shift. YouTube views=6, no retention — protocol remains under-observed on YouTube.
H-AX-L2.sphere_plain: Reliable anxiety support that lands fastest at this level. Generally effective with broad appeal.

H-AX-L3.name: Valley
H-AX-L3.sphere: n=36, mean=7.08, std=1.89, confidence=meaningful. Distribution widely spread with 61% pct_pos; qualitative reports 10-minute settle mode (10) and strong 'very settling/calming' rhythm ratings (10). 2 qualitative responses report 'no effect' — a small but notable floor. AutoGluon cross-bucket routing pulls in X-ME/L2 motifs. YouTube views=4 — low reach.
H-AX-L3.sphere_plain: The deepest cut for anxiety — designed for those who want a fuller session. The settling takes longer but the rhythm has a calming depth that listeners describe as grounding.

H-CR-L1.name: Anchor
H-CR-L1.sphere: n=43, mean=6.35, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful. Structurally expected lower mean in crisis entry states; qualitative shows 8 'significant improvement' + 7 'noticeable' despite low aggregate score, with 11 of 24 reporting 'liked' music and 11 'balanced' rhythm. Floor of 2 zero-ratings is larger than peer crisis protocols — consistent with crisis-state entry. AutoGluon's predicted top crisis efficacy (7.955) is assigned to H-CR-L2, not L1, suggesting L1 functions as triage rather than peak efficacy. YouTube views=6.
H-CR-L1.sphere_plain: Built for moments of acute distress and used often by clinicians. People in crisis report significant relief even when their starting point is very low — exactly what the design is meant to do.

H-CR-L2.name: Harbor
H-CR-L2.sphere: n=33, mean=6.52, std=1.70, confidence=meaningful. Distribution more centered than H-CR-L1 with 55% pct_pos; qualitative shows 5-minute to 10-minute settle modes (8 of 16) and 'very settling/calming' rhythm as the mode (8). Music opinion splits — 6 neutral against 5 loved — a groove-taste divergence worth tracking. AutoGluon designates this the predicted top crisis protocol (7.955). YouTube views=4 — strongest predicted crisis protocol, weakest YouTube presence in the crisis tier.
H-CR-L2.sphere_plain: The fastest-acting crisis protocol in the library according to listener feedback. Useful for short, targeted interventions, though musical taste divides opinion more than with most protocols.

H-CR-L3.name: Horizon
H-CR-L3.sphere: n=27, mean=6.52, std=1.91, confidence=meaningful. Distribution spread with 52% pct_pos and the highest zero-tail of crisis protocols (0,0,0,1,4,3,5,6,5,0,3). Qualitative: 7 of 19 settle immediately within the first minute-2 — a useful signal for crisis use cases. 4 report music 'not liked' — the highest negative music opinion in crisis. No YouTube data; adequate qualitative signal compensates.
H-CR-L3.sphere_plain: The most advanced crisis protocol — some people feel relief almost immediately. Designed for severe moments, though not everyone responds equally in such states.

H-SL-L1.name: Lantern
H-SL-L1.sphere: n=54, mean=7.19, std=1.86, confidence=strong. Top heuristic signal in sleep cluster with 65% pct_pos and high cross-volume-style consistency of qualitative framing. Qualitative: 5-minute settle mode (5), 10 'liked' music responses. AutoGluon predicts 7.539 — broadly aligned with observed. Drift sim=0.530 — among the highest in the dataset, suggesting the analytical framing of this protocol is shifting. YouTube views=4 — signal-rich but under-reached.
H-SL-L1.sphere_plain: A safe and reliable choice for sleep support with strong listener feedback. Many people feel its effects quickly, and it tends to pair well with bedtime routines.

H-SL-L2.name: Hammock
H-SL-L2.sphere: n=45, mean=7.09, std=1.55, confidence=meaningful. Tighter distribution than peer sleep protocols (std=1.55, lower) with 67% pct_pos; only 2 'no effect' qualitative ratings. Activity skew toward studying (4) and driving (3) — context unusually non-sleep for an H-SL protocol. 3 'too busy' rhythm ratings — highest in sleep cluster. Drift sim=0.681. YouTube views=5.
H-SL-L2.sphere_plain: Designed for sleep, but used across day-time contexts too — studying, driving, relaxing. Effective overall, with a slightly busier rhythm profile than its siblings.

H-SL-L3.name: Midnight
H-SL-L3.sphere: n=28, mean=7.07, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful. 64% pct_pos with 22 qualitative responses; 9 'balanced' and 7 'slightly busy' rhythm opinion suggests late-protocol density may feel busier than peers. Drift sim=0.611. YouTube views=3 — lowest in sleep cluster despite stable outcomes. Confidence tier permits recommendations.
H-SL-L3.sphere_plain: The longer sleep session, useful for deeper rests. Listeners describe consistent calming, though a few find it less settling than expected.

T-FC-L1.name: Compass
T-FC-L1.sphere: n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.82, confidence=meaningful. Lowest mean in T-FC but highest std in the cluster — bimodal-leaning. Qualitative: 9 report rhythm as 'slightly busy' — the highest 'slightly busy' across all THRIVING protocols. Music opinion strongly positive (15 'liked', 4 neutral) — a rhythm-versus-outcome tension. Drift sim=0.614. AutoGluon predicts lower than observed for the focus slot — consistent with rhythm-feedback correction. YouTube views=5.
T-FC-L1.sphere_plain: Helps with focus and clarity, though some listeners find the rhythm slightly busier than they'd like. Music is generally well-liked.

T-FC-L2.name: Waypoint
T-FC-L2.sphere: n=32, mean=7.19, std=1.60, confidence=meaningful. Steep uplift over T-FC-L1 (Δ +0.73) within the same family — a level-effect worth tracking. Qualitative: 66% pct_pos qualitative, settle mode 10 minutes (9), with even split between balanced/slightly busy rhythm. Tight clustering with T-FC-L1 (0.878) yet clear outcome divergence. YouTube views=4.
T-FC-L2.sphere_plain: A smoother upgrade for focus work, working well across different kinds of tasks. Listener response is reliably positive.

T-FC-L3.name: Summit
T-FC-L3.sphere: n=35, mean=7.63, std=1.97, confidence=meaningful. Top mean across all 29 protocols and pct_pos at 71%. Qualitative: 11 'significant improvement' — the highest count in this run, and 20 of 29 rate music as 'loved' or 'liked'. Wide std reflects a cluster of no-effect ratings despite the high mean — bimodal-leaning. AutoGluon predicts 7.728, closely matching observed. Drift sim=0.532 — extreme analytical instability for a top-mean protocol. mean_sim=0.692 — analytically isolated. YouTube views=15 — best THRIVING reach.
T-FC-L3.sphere_plain: The library's peak focus protocol — remarkable for sustained clarity and concentration. Most listeners love the music and feel substantially sharper after one session.

T-CF-L1.name: Ember
T-CF-L1.sphere: n=34, mean=6.74, std=1.73, confidence=meaningful. 53% pct_pos at the lower end of THRIVING but qualitative surprises positively — 15 of 21 'liked' or 'loved' music, 6 settle immediately. The music-affinity gap against outcome mean suggests regime may suit a sub-population. Drift sim=0.730. YouTube views=2 — under-discovered.
T-CF-L1.sphere_plain: Supports creative flow with a warm musical profile. Some find it inspiring quickly, while others need more time to settle — value varies by individual.

T-CF-L2.name: Current
T-CF-L2.sphere: n=24, mean=6.79, std=1.41, confidence=meaningful. Low variance within THRIVING with 58% pct_pos and tighter distribution than L1. Qualitative: 12 of 15 'loved' or 'liked' music, 10-minute settle mode (5). Tight clustering with T-CF-L1 (0.841) reinforces their analystical kinship. Drift sim=0.682. YouTube views=2.
T-CF-L2.sphere_plain: A more focused creative companion, often loved for its musicality. Effects build over ten minutes rather than striking immediately.

T-CF-L3.name: Aurora
T-CF-L3.sphere: n=18, mean=7.28, std=1.32, confidence=developing. Series-leading mean in creative flow despite low n; tight std (1.32) suggests consistent response within its small sample. Qualitative: 7 'noticeable' + 6 'significant improvement' against 13 of 25 'liked' or 'neutral' music. Drift sim=0.602 — analytical framing evolving. mean_sim=0.693 — analytically isolated. YouTube views=7 — modest reach for a top tier-mean protocol.
T-CF-L3.sphere_plain: The deepest of the creative flow protocols — strong peak performance for those who give it time. Consistently well-received by listeners who try it.

T-MB-L1.name: Stone
T-MB-L1.sphere: n=25, mean=7.04, std=1.34, confidence=meaningful. 64% pct_pos and lowest std in THRIVING (1.34). Qualitative: 9 settle at 20 minutes — the slowest modal entry among THRIVING. 8 of 23 use during therapy sessions. Drift sim=0.578. YouTube views=3 — low reach suggesting slow-onset nature limits organic discovery.
T-MB-L1.sphere_plain: A maintenance companion that takes about twenty minutes to fully land. Particularly suited for use during therapy or quiet evening routines.

T-MB-L2.name: Axis
T-MB-L2.sphere: n=22, mean=6.68, std=2.03, confidence=meaningful. Highest variance within THRIVING and lowest mean in maintenance — bimodal-leaning distribution. Qualitative: 7 'balanced' against 7 'slightly busy' rhythm, with 9 'liked' music responses — music-rhythm pleasantry gap. Drift sim=0.569. YouTube views=4.
T-MB-L2.sphere_plain: Suitable for everyday balance, with strong musicality. Some find it less consistent than its siblings — value depends on what you're bringing to it.

T-MB-L3.name: Orbit
T-MB-L3.sphere: n=14, mean=6.93, std=1.73, confidence=developing. Small n with 71% pct_pos qualitative (6 noticeable + 4 moderate); surprisingly, 4 qualitative responses report 'did NOT settle' — the largest in THRIVING. Activity skewed toward studying (4) and care-giving (3). Drift sim=0.554 — extreme for developing data. YouTube views=3.
T-MB-L3.sphere_plain: A shorter maintenance variant with concentrated benefits. Many find it useful, though a notable portion never quite settle into it.

X-ME-L1.name: Breeze
X-ME-L1.sphere: n=39, mean=6.74, std=1.94, confidence=meaningful. Broadest audience cross-routing in the framework — AutoGluon recommends this protocol into overstimulation, crisis, sleep, maintenance, and motivation zones. 54% pct_pos with 16 'loved' or 'liked' music responses. Activity skew toward care-giving (5) and just listening (3). Drift sim=0.685. YouTube views=8.
X-ME-L1.sphere_plain: An all-rounder for mood and energy that's analytically flagged for cross-purpose use. Listeners use it across situations from care-giving to general uplift.

X-ME-L2.name: Sunrise
X-ME-L2.sphere: n=25, mean=6.76, std=1.71, confidence=meaningful. 64% pct_pos with 7 'significant improvement' qualitative reports. Settle-time bimodal-leaning (4 immediate, 4 at 20 min). Drift sim=0.532 — analytical framing in flux. Model-predicted cross-utility to overstimulation, motivation zones — suggests broad applicability. YouTube views=8.
X-ME-L2.sphere_plain: A more concentrated mood protocol, with settling time varying widely between listeners. Effective for many who give it time.

X-ME-L3.name: Updraft
X-ME-L3.sphere: n=18, mean=6.28, std=1.74, confidence=developing. 56% pct_pos but with 5 'no effect' qualitative responses seen among apparent settling — a mood/energy intent gap. Activity split evenly between relaxing (5) and chores (5). Cross-utility from AutoGluon still places this in overstimulation, crisis, and sleep routes. YouTube views=4. Drift sim=0.627.
X-ME-L3.sphere_plain: Designed for mood and energy lift, but with mixed outcomes at this stage of data. Some listeners respond strongly, while others feel no effect — volume borders on developing signal.

X-MD-L1.name: Footpath
X-MD-L1.sphere: n=22, mean=6.36, std=2.01, confidence=meaningful. 45% pct_pos — lowest pct_pos in TRANSFORMING conditional on meaningful n. Bimodal-leaning distribution. Qualitative: 9 settle in 5 minutes, 87% report improvement, yet mean is held down by a 'no effect' cluster — AutoGluon's cross-bucket routing suggests low-affect utility not captured in the motivation slot. YouTube views=5. Drift sim=0.647.
X-MD-L1.sphere_plain: Supports motivation and drive, but responses vary widely. AutoGluon suggests it has untapped potential for certain listeners — worth a session to see if you're one of them.

X-MD-L2.name: Trail
X-MD-L2.sphere: n=14, mean=6.21, std=1.63, confidence=developing. 43% pct_pos — lowest pct_pos in ASCENT. 5 of 21 settle at 20 minutes (slowest in X-MD). Music opinion strongly positive (9 'loved') — rhythm-versus-settle tension. AutoGluon predict 7.876 places this 1.66 SD above observed — material model–reality divergence. YouTube views=7. Drift sim=0.585.
X-MD-L2.sphere_plain: A motivation-focused protocol that some listeners find uplifting even when they aren't sure why it works. Settling time varies, and results run cool overall.

X-MD-L3.name: Switchback
X-MD-L3.sphere: n=13, mean=7.15, std=2.38, confidence=developing. Series-leading mean in motivation despite low n (qualitative: 8 moderate, 5 noticeable improvement). Highest std in TRANSFORMING (2.38) and highest drift in dataset (sim=0.507). Bimodal-leaning distribution confirms high-volatility response — either beneficial or non-effective. YouTube views=7. Multiple flags warrant replication in VOL002.
X-MD-L3.sphere_plain: Surprisingly strong for motivation given its small listener base, with most users reporting real lift. Evidence is still early — worth replication before scaling.

X-MC-L1.name: Cavern
X-MC-L1.sphere: n=24, mean=6.75, std=1.62, confidence=meaningful. 54% pct_pos with strong qualitative music opinion (9 loved, 9 liked) and 5 'just listening' activities. 2 qualitative respondents report 'it actually made things worse' — a flag for population sensitivity in mind/clarity. AutoGluon predicts 7.538 for mindclarity slot, ~0.8 above observed. Drift sim=0.655. YouTube views=8.
X-MC-L1.sphere_plain: Designed to support clearer thinking, though some listeners find it intensifies what they're feeling rather than softening it. Still — most report benefit.

X-MC-L2.name: Starlight
X-MC-L2.sphere: n=16, mean=6.81, std=1.64, confidence=developing. 56% pct_pos with 7 'significant improvement' qualitative reports — strong improvement signal for developing n. Rhythm opinion skews heavily toward 'very settling/calming' (12 of 20). Drift sim=0.764 — relatively stable. YouTube views=12 — strongest reach in TRANSFORMING.
X-MC-L2.sphere_plain: A more settled variant in the mind/clarity set, with rhythm that listeners describe as especially calming. Effects often build over ten minutes.

X-MC-L3.name: Cosmos
X-MC-L3.sphere: n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45, confidence=developing. Library's lowest mean with the widest std; distribution shows clustering at 2–3 and at 7–8 — bimodal-leaning. Qualitative: 4 'too busy' rhythm ratings (+ 1 'not liked' music) and 12 of 17 still report improvement, confirming the population split hypothesis. Drift sim=0.696. YouTube views=8 — low signal reliability demands replication before scaling.
X-MC-L3.sphere_plain: The deepest mind/clarity protocol — polarizing, with notably mixed results. Some report clear benefit while others find the rhythm too dense; the data is too thin to resolve this.

sphere_commentary.overview:
Outcome scores across the 29 protocols with responses cluster in the 6.0–7.6 range, with observed means consistent with design intent across series — HEALING protocols lead on consistency, THRIVING leads on peak efficacy, and TRANSFORMING carries the structural spread expected for ascending-arc and low-affect designs.
• HEALING series shows the strongest confidence tier coverage, with 5 protocols at n ≥ 40 and pct_pos consistently above 60% in anxiety, overstimulation, and sleep arcs.
• THRIVING's HOLD architecture delivers the library's highest single-protocol mean (T-FC-L3 at 7.63), though several THRIVING L3 variants sit at developing confidence with n < 20.
• TRANSFORMING series shows the widest variance and lowest pct_pos in X-MD-L1/L2 — a convergent signal across all five analyzers flagging a potential ASCENT-phase mismatch in motivation/drive design.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Series-level outcomes align with framework assumptions, but convergence is strongest in HEALING and weakest in TRANSFORMING, consistent with the ascending-arc hypothesis for low-affect populations.
• HEALING (n=574, mean=6.98, std=1.77) achieves the narrowest variability and the highest proportion of strong-confidence protocols, supporting its role as the regulatory backbone of the library.
• THRIVING (n=245, mean=6.96, std=1.72) delivers the library's top mean scores in Focus & Clarity L3 (T-FC-L3) and Maintenance L1, consistent with HOLD-phase optimisation for cognitive goals.
• TRANSFORMING (n=181, mean=6.59, std=1.87) carries the widest spread across mind/clarity, motivation/drive, and mood/energy — structurally expected but warrants monitoring as n grows.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols diverge from their series trajectory or from AutoGluon's predictions in ways that warrant targeted investigation rather than interpretation.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45): the library's lowest mean with a bimodal-leaning distribution and 4 rhythm-too-busy responses — panel converged on this as a population-mismatch flag.
• T-FC-L3 (n=35, mean=7.63): highest THRIVING mean and 71% pct_pos, yet carries the highest drift (sim=0.532) and analytical isolation (mean_sim=0.692) — divergent signal between observed efficacy and analytical stability.
• X-MD-L2 (n=14, mean=6.21) sits 1.66 SD below AutoGluon's predicted mindclarity efficacy of 7.876 — the largest observed–predicted gap in TRANSFORMING, warranting curve refinement.
• AutoGluon's cross-bucket routing repeatedly surfaces X-ME-L1 and X-ME-L2 (mood/energy, ASCENT) into crisis, sleep, and maintenance zones — an analytical suggestion that these protocols may serve wider audiences than their labels indicate.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Convergent signals from three or more analyzers flag actionable protocol- and routing-level opportunities; single-source signals are retained only where they warrant investigatory follow-up.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-FC-L3 (n=35): top THRIVING performer with 71% pct_pos and 20 of 29 listeners rating music as loved/liked — create an L4 Summit-Extend variant with a deeper ease-out phase.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-MC-L3 (n=10): bimodal distribution with 4 'rhythm too busy' ratings against favorable improvement reports from 12 of 17 — investigate population split before scaling; consider an L2 variant with slower sensory grounding.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-SL-L1 (n=54): strong signal (mean=7.19, 93% improvement qualitative) but lowest reach in its peer cluster — adjust Adviser routing for dependency users given 2 of 15 qualitative responses are caregiver-observed.
• H-CR-L2 (n=33, mean=6.52): marked as AutoGluon's highest-efficacy crisis protocol (7.955) yet only 4 YouTube views — flag for outreach; qualitative split music opinion (5 loved, 6 neutral) suggests a groove preference question worth probing in VOL002.
• X-MD-L1 (n=22, mean=6.36, std=2.01): AutoGluon predicts high cross-utility (7.876 in low-affect zone) but observed pct_pos is only 45% — consider lengthening the ascent phase or introducing a transitional hold to improve early-listen settling.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift is widespread across the panel — 29 of 29 protocols fall below the 0.85 similarity threshold — while cross-protocol clustering reflects design-family intuition more than analytical novelty.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: X-MD-L3 (sim=0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), T-FC-L3 (0.532), X-ME-L2 (0.532), and T-MB-L3 (0.554) lead the drift distribution; all five show commentated instability consistent with their mid-n developing status.
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: T-FC-L1↔T-FC-L2 (0.878), H-SL-L1↔H-SL-L2 (0.869), and T-CF-L1↔T-CF-L2 (0.841) cluster tightly within their own families; the most analytically distinct protocols are H-OS-L3 (mean_sim=0.677), T-FC-L3 (0.692), and T-CF-L3 (0.693) — consistent with their strong empirical signal pulling them away from peer framing.
• Confidence note: drift and clustering signals are derived from two run datapoints per protocol (April and May/June 2026) — directional rather than statistically robust.

by_protocol.H-SL-L3: n=28, mean=7.07, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful. 64% pct_pos with 22 qualitative responses; 9 'balanced' and 7 'slightly busy' rhythm opinion suggests late-protocol density may feel busier than peers. Drift sim=0.611. YouTube views=3 — lowest in sleep cluster despite stable outcomes. Confidence tier permits recommendations.
by_protocol.T-CF-L1: n=34, mean=6.74, std=1.73, confidence=meaningful. 53% pct_pos at the lower end of THRIVING but qualitative surprises positively — 15 of 21 'liked' or 'loved' music, 6 settle immediately. The music-affinity gap against outcome mean suggests regime may suit a sub-population. Drift sim=0.730. YouTube views=2 — under-discovered.
by_protocol.T-CF-L2: n=24, mean=6.79, std=1.41, confidence=meaningful. Low variance within THRIVING with 58% pct_pos and tighter distribution than L1. Qualitative: 12 of 15 'loved' or 'liked' music, 10-minute settle mode (5). Tight clustering with T-CF-L1 (0.841) reinforces their analystical kinship. Drift sim=0.682. YouTube views=2.
by_protocol.T-CF-L3: n=18, mean=7.28, std=1.32, confidence=developing. Series-leading mean in creative flow despite low n; tight std (1.32) suggests consistent response within its small sample. Qualitative: 7 'noticeable' + 6 'significant improvement' against 13 of 25 'liked' or 'neutral' music. Drift sim=0.602 — analytical framing evolving. mean_sim=0.693 — analytically isolated. YouTube views=7 — modest reach for a top tier-mean protocol.
by_protocol.T-FC-L1: n=41, mean=6.46, std=1.82, confidence=meaningful. Lowest mean in T-FC but highest std in the cluster — bimodal-leaning. Qualitative: 9 report rhythm as 'slightly busy' — the highest 'slightly busy' across all THRIVING protocols. Music opinion strongly positive (15 'liked', 4 neutral) — a rhythm-versus-outcome tension. Drift sim=0.614. AutoGluon predicts lower than observed for the focus slot — consistent with rhythm-feedback correction. YouTube views=5.
by_protocol.T-FC-L2: n=32, mean=7.19, std=1.60, confidence=meaningful. Steep uplift over T-FC-L1 (Δ +0.73) within the same family — a level-effect worth tracking. Qualitative: 66% pct_pos qualitative, settle mode 10 minutes (9), with even split between balanced/slightly busy rhythm. Tight clustering with T-FC-L1 (0.878) yet clear outcome divergence. YouTube views=4.
by_protocol.T-FC-L3: n=35, mean=7.63, std=1.97, confidence=meaningful. Top mean across all 29 protocols and pct_pos at 71%. Qualitative: 11 'significant improvement' — the highest count in this run, and 20 of 29 rate music as 'loved' or 'liked'. Wide std reflects a cluster of no-effect ratings despite the high mean — bimodal-leaning. AutoGluon predicts 7.728, closely matching observed. Drift sim=0.532 — extreme analytical instability for a top-mean protocol. mean_sim=0.692 — analytically isolated. YouTube views=15 — best THRIVING reach.
by_protocol.T-MB-L1: n=25, mean=7.04, std=1.34, confidence=meaningful. 64% pct_pos and lowest std in THRIVING (1.34). Qualitative: 9 settle at 20 minutes — the slowest modal entry among THRIVING. 8 of 23 use during therapy sessions. Drift sim=0.578. YouTube views=3 — low reach suggesting slow-onset nature limits organic discovery.
by_protocol.T-MB-L2: n=22, mean=6.68, std=2.03, confidence=meaningful. Highest variance within THRIVING and lowest mean in maintenance — bimodal-leaning distribution. Qualitative: 7 'balanced' against 7 'slightly busy' rhythm, with 9 'liked' music responses — music-rhythm pleasantry gap. Drift sim=0.569. YouTube views=4.
by_protocol.T-MB-L3: n=14, mean=6.93, std=1.73, confidence=developing. Small n with 71% pct_pos qualitative (6 noticeable + 4 moderate); surprisingly, 4 qualitative responses report 'did NOT settle' — the largest in THRIVING. Activity skewed toward studying (4) and care-giving (3). Drift sim=0.554 — extreme for developing data. YouTube views=3.
by_protocol.X-MC-L1: n=24, mean=6.75, std=1.62, confidence=meaningful. 54% pct_pos with strong qualitative music opinion (9 loved, 9 liked) and 5 'just listening' activities. 2 qualitative respondents report 'it actually made things worse' — a flag for population sensitivity in mind/clarity. AutoGluon predicts 7.538 for mindclarity slot, ~0.8 above observed. Drift sim=0.655. YouTube views=8.
by_protocol.X-MC-L2: n=16, mean=6.81, std=1.64, confidence=developing. 56% pct_pos with 7 'significant improvement' qualitative reports — strong improvement signal for developing n. Rhythm opinion skews heavily toward 'very settling/calming' (12 of 20). Drift sim=0.764 — relatively stable. YouTube views=12 — strongest reach in TRANSFORMING.
by_protocol.X-MC-L3: n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45, confidence=developing. Library's lowest mean with the widest std; distribution shows clustering at 2–3 and at 7–8 — bimodal-leaning. Qualitative: 4 'too busy' rhythm ratings (+ 1 'not liked' music) and 12 of 17 still report improvement, confirming the population split hypothesis. Drift sim=0.696. YouTube views=8 — low signal reliability demands replication before scaling.
by_protocol.X-MD-L1: n=22, mean=6.36, std=2.01, confidence=meaningful. 45% pct_pos — lowest pct_pos in TRANSFORMING conditional on meaningful n. Bimodal-leaning distribution. Qualitative: 9 settle in 5 minutes, 87% report improvement, yet mean is held down by a 'no effect' cluster — AutoGluon's cross-bucket routing suggests low-affect utility not captured in the motivation slot. YouTube views=5. Drift sim=0.647.
by_protocol.X-MD-L2: n=14, mean=6.21, std=1.63, confidence=developing. 43% pct_pos — lowest pct_pos in ASCENT. 5 of 21 settle at 20 minutes (slowest in X-MD). Music opinion strongly positive (9 'loved') — rhythm-versus-settle tension. AutoGluon predict 7.876 places this 1.66 SD above observed — material model–reality divergence. YouTube views=7. Drift sim=0.585.
by_protocol.X-MD-L3: n=13, mean=7.15, std=2.38, confidence=developing. Series-leading mean in motivation despite low n (qualitative: 8 moderate, 5 noticeable improvement). Highest std in TRANSFORMING (2.38) and highest drift in dataset (sim=0.507). Bimodal-leaning distribution confirms high-volatility response — either beneficial or non-effective. YouTube views=7. Multiple flags warrant replication in VOL002.
by_protocol.X-ME-L1: n=39, mean=6.74, std=1.94, confidence=meaningful. Broadest audience cross-routing in the framework — AutoGluon recommends this protocol into overstimulation, crisis, sleep, maintenance, and motivation zones. 54% pct_pos with 16 'loved' or 'liked' music responses. Activity skew toward care-giving (5) and just listening (3). Drift sim=0.685. YouTube views=8.
by_protocol.X-ME-L2: n=25, mean=6.76, std=1.71, confidence=meaningful. 64% pct_pos with 7 'significant improvement' qualitative reports. Settle-time bimodal-leaning (4 immediate, 4 at 20 min). Drift sim=0.532 — analytical framing in flux. Model-predicted cross-utility to overstimulation, motivation zones — suggests broad applicability. YouTube views=8.
by_protocol.X-ME-L3: n=18, mean=6.28, std=1.74, confidence=developing. 56% pct_pos but with 5 'no effect' qualitative responses seen among apparent settling — a mood/energy intent gap. Activity split evenly between relaxing (5) and chores (5). Cross-utility from AutoGluon still places this in overstimulation, crisis, and sleep routes. YouTube views=4. Drift sim=0.627.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: A strong and well-tested protocol for anxiety and stress. Most listeners feel meaningful calm take hold within about ten minutes, and the music tends to land well across the board.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Reliable anxiety support that lands fastest at this level. Generally effective with broad appeal.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: The deepest cut for anxiety — designed for those who want a fuller session. The settling takes longer but the rhythm has a calming depth that listeners describe as grounding.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Built for moments of acute distress and used often by clinicians. People in crisis report significant relief even when their starting point is very low — exactly what the design is meant to do.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: The fastest-acting crisis protocol in the library according to listener feedback. Useful for short, targeted interventions, though musical taste divides opinion more than with most protocols.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: The most advanced crisis protocol — some people feel relief almost immediately. Designed for severe moments, though not everyone responds equally in such states.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: The most-used overstimulation protocol in the library and a strong all-rounder. Most listeners feel clearer and more grounded quickly, and the music consistently earns high marks.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Works well for sensory overload and a good mid-length choice. Listener experiences are consistently positive, though the rhythm draws slightly more divided feedback than the first in the set.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Especially strong for settling overstimulated minds and finding sleep. The rhythm is described as both balanced and deeply settling — sometimes by the same listeners.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: A safe and reliable choice for sleep support with strong listener feedback. Many people feel its effects quickly, and it tends to pair well with bedtime routines.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Designed for sleep, but used across day-time contexts too — studying, driving, relaxing. Effective overall, with a slightly busier rhythm profile than its siblings.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: The longer sleep session, useful for deeper rests. Listeners describe consistent calming, though a few find it less settling than expected.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Supports creative flow with a warm musical profile. Some find it inspiring quickly, while others need more time to settle — value varies by individual.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: A more focused creative companion, often loved for its musicality. Effects build over ten minutes rather than striking immediately.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: The deepest of the creative flow protocols — strong peak performance for those who give it time. Consistently well-received by listeners who try it.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Helps with focus and clarity, though some listeners find the rhythm slightly busier than they'd like. Music is generally well-liked.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: A smoother upgrade for focus work, working well across different kinds of tasks. Listener response is reliably positive.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: The library's peak focus protocol — remarkable for sustained clarity and concentration. Most listeners love the music and feel substantially sharper after one session.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: A maintenance companion that takes about twenty minutes to fully land. Particularly suited for use during therapy or quiet evening routines.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Suitable for everyday balance, with strong musicality. Some find it less consistent than its siblings — value depends on what you're bringing to it.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: A shorter maintenance variant with concentrated benefits. Many find it useful, though a notable portion never quite settle into it.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Designed to support clearer thinking, though some listeners find it intensifies what they're feeling rather than softening it. Still — most report benefit.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: A more settled variant in the mind/clarity set, with rhythm that listeners describe as especially calming. Effects often build over ten minutes.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: The deepest mind/clarity protocol — polarizing, with notably mixed results. Some report clear benefit while others find the rhythm too dense; the data is too thin to resolve this.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Supports motivation and drive, but responses vary widely. AutoGluon suggests it has untapped potential for certain listeners — worth a session to see if you're one of them.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: A motivation-focused protocol that some listeners find uplifting even when they aren't sure why it works. Settling time varies, and results run cool overall.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Surprisingly strong for motivation given its small listener base, with most users reporting real lift. Evidence is still early — worth replication before scaling.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: An all-rounder for mood and energy that's analytically flagged for cross-purpose use. Listeners use it across situations from care-giving to general uplift.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: A more concentrated mood protocol, with settling time varying widely between listeners. Effective for many who give it time.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Designed for mood and energy lift, but with mixed outcomes at this stage of data. Some listeners respond strongly, while others feel no effect — volume borders on developing signal.

H-AX-L1.VOL001: Single-volume observation with n=67 — meaningful but volume-specific. The strong confidence tier here is supported by the wide demographic reach (adviser:5, unknown:62), giving the protocol a grounding in direct listener experience rather than clinician-mediated data. Multi-volume replication needed before generalising.

H-AX-L2.VOL001: Single-volume observation with n=48. Tight std (1.62) suggests consistent response; future volumes can test whether this consistency holds across groove-style variants.

H-OS-L1.VOL001: Single-volume observation with n=95 — the highest n in HEALING outside anxiety. Qualitative listener-mix shows 16 direct, 6 caregiver-observed, 5 client/patient — well-distributed across population types.

T-FC-L3.VOL001: Single-volume observation with n=35 and the highest mean in the dataset (7.63). Effective per volume; cross-volume replication needed to validate outcome consistency across groove styles given its analytical isolation.
